title: The night prayer
hook: prayer after sleeping and waking in the night

segments.voice: Yesterday, witr: the odd prayer that closes the night. Today we stay in the night.

A quarter past three in the morning. The house is dark, the phone face-down, the fridge humming to itself. Someone gets out of a warm bed, not because a baby cried or a dream went wrong. On purpose. Cold water on the hands and face for wudu. A mat unrolled in the corner of the bedroom. No adhan calls this prayer. Nobody at the mosque will notice who came. The street is asleep, and that's part of the point. It's a prayer you go to sleep before, and then get up for.
screen: `A QUARTER PAST THREE.` → `UP ON PURPOSE.` → `NO ADHAN CALLS THIS ONE.`

segments.voice: Tahajjud is the voluntary prayer of the night, prayed after you've slept and woken. First, the Qur'an, where it begins as words to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ himself. Pickthall's translation of surah seventeen: "And some part of the night awake for it, a largess for thee." A largess: a gift beyond what was owed. The five daily prayers are the duty; this one is the gift on top. Second, the people the Qur'an describes, in surah thirty-two: those "Who forsake their beds to cry unto their Lord in fear and hope." It's an honest picture. The bed is warm, and leaving it costs something. Third, why the dark hours. A hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari says that every night, when its last third remains, God asks: who is calling on Me, so that I may answer? Who is asking, so that I may give? Who seeks forgiveness, so that I may forgive? Some readers hear the timing as an invitation: the quietest hour is the one the hadith describes as open. Fourth, one life. Aisha, his wife, saw the Prophet stand in the night prayer until his feet swelled, and asked why, when he had already been forgiven. He answered with a question: should I not be a grateful servant? The night prayer isn't a debt paid down. It's thanks. And since the hadith asks that witr be the last of the night's prayer, tahajjud comes first, and the night still closes odd. Some keep it often, some in hard seasons, some in Ramadan, some rarely. The gift is described the same way for all of them.
screen: `A LARGESS: THE GIFT ON TOP.` · `THEY FORSAKE THEIR BEDS.` · `WHO IS CALLING ON ME?` · `SHOULD I NOT BE GRATEFUL?` · then, large: `AND SOME PART OF THE NIGHT AWAKE FOR IT.`

segments.voice: Picture one night this week when you might wake: the dark room, the cold water, the corner where you'd stand. If you pray, set your intention now to rise after sleeping and pray two units. If you don't, you might set an alarm a few minutes early and spend them awake and quiet, before the day gets a say.
Tahajjud. The voluntary night prayer, prayed after sleeping and waking, a gift beyond the duty. Today's word.
Your line: awake for him. The night prayer is thanks, not a debt. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Muslims who keep tahajjud usually sleep first, then rise in the later part of the night, make wudu and pray voluntary units in pairs, often finishing with witr before the dawn prayer.
